factual_objections.claim: A good monthly churn rate typically falls between three and seven percent.
factual_objections.evidence: For the requested Hormozi benchmark, the packet gives Skool's average as 20% monthly churn and the best groups as under 10%. It explicitly identifies substituting 3–7% benchmarks as an error.
factual_objections.label: contradicted

factual_objections.claim: A monthly churn rate above ten percent is alarming and signals broken onboarding, unmet value expectations, or poor member fit.
factual_objections.evidence: The supplied benchmark averages 20% churn, with retention becoming the highest-ROI priority around 30% churn or higher. Elevated early churn is described as normal unless almost everyone leaves, so exceeding 10% does not establish a broken process.
factual_objections.label: contradicted

factual_objections.claim: Hormozi contends that members will not leave if they receive ten times their subscription cost in value within the first week.
factual_objections.evidence: The packet supports early outcomes and onboarding, but supplies no ten-times-value threshold or guarantee that members will stay.
factual_objections.label: unverified

factual_objections.claim: If churn exceeds eight percent for two consecutive months, pause marketing spend entirely.
factual_objections.evidence: The supplied material establishes no eight-percent threshold, two-month rule, or instruction to stop marketing entirely.
factual_objections.label: unverified

verdict.reason: A substantially matches the 20% average, roughly 30% intervention threshold, tenure effects, and young-community caveat. It should distinguish average from good, mention that the best groups churn under 10%, and give the approximately 10% post-day-90 benchmark. B substitutes incompatible benchmarks and unsupported intervention rules that could cause unnecessary cuts to acquisition.
